executive_summary.question: What punishment applies to abetment of an offence when the Sanhita makes no express provision for punishing that specific abetment?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 contains **no express provision** for punishing a particular act of abetment, the law falls back on the following rules (as set out in the Sanhita itself): | Situation | Punishment (when no express provision exists) | Source | |-----------|-----------------------------------------------|--------| | **The act abetted is actually committed** (i.e., the offence occurs because of the abetment) | The abettor receives **the same punishment as the principal offender** for that offence. | Section 49 – “Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, … be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.”【e3cfd376-1174-46eb-9573-2b6cafe0dbc6】 | | **The offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life is *not* committed** (abetment only) | Imprisonment of either description for a term **up to seven years**, **plus fine**.
If, in consequence of the abetment, any hurt is caused to a person, the term may extend to **fourteen years**, **plus fine**. | Section 55 (illustrated in the text) – “Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life … shall be punished with imprisonment … which may extend to seven years … and if any hurt be done … imprisonment … which may extend to fourteen years … and shall also be liable to fine.”【320c1526-fed5-4985-ae85-e16910f24ab6】 | | **The offence is punishable with imprisonment (but not death or life)** and is *not* committed | Imprisonment of any description provided for that offence, for a term **up to one‑fourth of the longest term** prescribed for the offence, **or** such fine as is provided for the offence, **or both**.
If the abettor (or the person abetted) is a public servant whose duty it is to prevent the offence, the term may extend to **one‑half** of the longest term (instead of one‑fourth), with the same fine option. | Section 56 – “Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment … shall be punished with imprisonment … for a term which may extend to one‑fourth part of the longest term …; … if the abettor … is a public servant … imprisonment … for a term which may extend to one‑half of the longest term ….”【a90a5461-96e5-4ff3-b754-c6e6c504fe4e】 | **In short:** - If the abetted act actually happens → punishment mirrors that of the offence. - If it does **not** happen → the Sanhita prescribes a reduced term (7 years / 14 years if hurt for death/life‑imprisonment offences; one‑fourth of the maximum term, or one‑half for public servants, for ordinary imprisonment offences), together with a fine where applicable. These rules apply whenever the Sanhita lacks a specific punishment clause for the particular abetment.
